c.tagline: A fourth 'holy city' of Islam behind ancient walls, famous for its 82 mosques and nightly hyena-feeding tradition

card: Rarely accepted; cash is essential throughout

taxi.fareNote: Bajaj tuk-tuks are the standard way around town; agree the fare before departure

emergency.note: English-language emergency support is limited; hotels can assist in arranging help

religion: Islam (Sunni majority, historically one of Islam's holiest cities)
walk: The walled Old City (Jugol) is a maze of narrow lanes best explored slowly on foot; outlying sites like Kondudo require a car

safety.safety: Generally safe and welcoming to visitors; the hyena feeding is conducted by experienced local handlers
safety.crime: Low crime in the old city; persistent unofficial guides are the main hassle

hood_landmark.Jugol (Walled Old City): Jugol's maze of narrow lanes and colorful traditional houses
hood_landmark.Ferez Magala Square: Ferez Magala, the square at the heart of Harar's mosque cluster

avoid.reason: The walled old city itself is fine, but check current security advice before overland travel in the wider eastern region.
Expect persistent would-be guides and hustle around the markets and gates, plus petty theft in crowded lanes — agree guide fees up front.

hood_desc: The historic walled core of Harar, a UNESCO-listed maze of narrow alleys, colorful houses, and dozens of mosques and shrines.
The bustling square at the heart of the old city, ringed by mosques and a good base for wandering the surrounding lanes.
A museum covering Harari culture, crafts, and history, useful context before exploring the old city itself.

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water only.

transit.hours: Roughly daylight to late evening (the hyena feeding happens after dark)
transit.map: Not centrally published; hotels arrange guides and transport
transit.note: A local guide is recommended for navigating the maze-like lanes of the old walled city

transport.air: Dire Dawa Aba Tenna Dejazmach Yilma International Airport (DIR), about 1 hr away, is the nearest airport
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Harar
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to Addis Ababa (about 9-10 hr) and Dire Dawa
transport.car: Well connected via road from Dire Dawa; most international visitors fly into Dire Dawa and drive

airport.name: Dire Dawa Aba Tenna Dejazmach Yilma International Airport

net.w: Wifi available in some hotels but often slow
net.fwn: Wifi available in central hotels, though unreliable
net.ap: An Ethio Telecom prepaid SIM, registered with your passport

tip.s: 10% is customary and expected for local guides and hyena-feeding handlers

landmarks: Harar Jugol (Old Walled City)
Islam's celebrated fourth-holiest city packs 82 mosques and countless shrines inside 16th-century walls, a UNESCO-listed maze of turquoise-and-pink alleyways.
Hyena Feeding at the City Gates
Each night outside the walls, Harar's famous hyena men hand-feed wild spotted hyenas by mouth, continuing a mesmerizing tradition of coexistence centuries old.
Arthur Rimbaud House (Rimbaud Cultural Center)
A gorgeous carved-wood merchant mansion honors the French poet-turned-trader who lived in Harar, displaying vintage photographs of the city from its upper gallery.
Grand Jami Mosque (Al-Jami Mosque)
Harar's whitewashed principal mosque, founded according to tradition in the 12th century, anchors the spiritual life of the old city's labyrinthine core.
Shoa Gate (Asmaddin Beri)
The busiest of Jugol's five historic gates funnels donkeys, spice sellers and shoppers through thick coral-stone walls into a whirl of market color.
Gidir Magala Market
Harar's central market overflows with sorted chilies, khat bundles, Harari baskets and shimmering fabrics, an intoxicating sensory plunge into eastern Ethiopian trade.
Sherif Harar City Museum
A passionate private collection of weaponry, coins, manuscripts and Harari jewelry, assembled by Abdullahi Sherif, chronicles the emirate's cosmopolitan trading history.
Harari Cultural House (Traditional Gey Gar)
Step inside a traditional Harari home whose crimson interior walls hang with woven baskets and eleven niches, explained by welcoming local custodians.
Medhane Alem Cathedral
Built on Feres Magala square after Menelik II's conquest, this octagonal Ethiopian Orthodox cathedral adds a Christian counterpoint to Harar's minaret-studded skyline.
Mekina Girgir (Sewing Machine Street)
Named for the whirring treadle machines of its tailors, this narrow photogenic lane epitomizes old Harar's craft traditions and irresistible alleyway atmosphere.

train.note: Harar itself has no station, but it is the closest of Ethiopia's historic towns to the working railway: the Addis Ababa-Djibouti standard-gauge line (https://bookingedr.et/) stops at Dire Dawa, about an hour away by road, with trains running roughly every second day. Book online with local mobile payment or at the station, and carry your passport.

bus.note: No scheduled international coaches from Harar - Djibouti and Somaliland are reached via Dire Dawa and Jijiga on regional and shared services. Selam Bus and Sky Bus run from Addis Ababa in about 10 hours, and minibuses shuttle constantly to Dire Dawa in an hour. Check current travel advice for eastern Ethiopia.

ferry.note: Harar is inland in the eastern highlands with no navigable water, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Dire Dawa
half.blurb: Railway town built by the Addis Ababa-Djibouti line, with a French colonial quarter and a large open-air market.

half.name: Babille Elephant Sanctuary
half.blurb: Protected dryland home to an isolated population of Ethiopian bush elephants, reachable by 4x4 from Harar.

full.name: Awash National Park
full.blurb: Rift Valley park along the Awash River with gorges, hot springs, and populations of oryx and gazelle.
